complexity_matrix.operation: Try one candidate value at depth d
complexity_matrix.notes: k is the constraint-check cost. O(1) when the check is incremental; O(k) when it rescans.

complexity_matrix.operation: Node count of the search tree (unpruned)
complexity_matrix.notes: b is branching, d is depth. Geometric in depth, so 2^30 is infeasible at a billion ops per second.

complexity_matrix.operation: Node count with pruning survival rate P
complexity_matrix.notes: Reducing P from 1 to 1/10 saves 10^d. Pruning dominates every other lever, exponentially.
b is approximately n per level. Useless without the legality tests.

complexity_matrix.operation: n-queens with column and diagonal pruning
complexity_matrix.notes: Growth rate established numerically; no proof of it exists. Still exponential in the worst case.

complexity_matrix.operation: Auxiliary space for the recursion stack plus partial solution
complexity_matrix.notes: Independent of nodes visited, because in-place mutation avoids a copy per level. This is what keeps space small.
Must traverse the entire tree. No early exit is available, unlike the any-solution variant.
Best case reaches a leaf immediately. The same algorithm may be exponentially cheaper than enumeration.
Scans columns and diagonals under attack. Total O(nodes * k).

complexity_matrix.operation: Constraint check per node, incremental counters
complexity_matrix.notes: Maintains per-column and per-diagonal counts. A factor-k gain, exponentially smaller than improving the prune rate.

complexity_matrix.operation: Memoised variant where two paths reach the same state
complexity_matrix.notes: S is the distinct state count. Exponential to polynomial. This is dynamic programming, not backtracking.

complexity_matrix.operation: Forward checking to a depth k constraint
complexity_matrix.notes: Detects inconsistency several levels ahead rather than where it appears, pruning strictly earlier.

correctness_argument.claim: Completeness holds by induction on decision depth: a valid solution S is never pruned because sound pruning cannot reject a valid prefix, and each level enumerates every candidate including S's. Soundness holds because each constraint is checked at the point it becomes determined. Distinctness of leaves follows because the loops at each depth enumerate distinct candidates.

cost_derivations.claim: Unpruned node count is Theta(b^d), a geometric sum. Pruning with survival rate P gives Theta((bP)^d), so pruning changes the base of the exponent rather than its degree, which is why it dominates per-node optimisation.
cost_derivations.detail: Auxiliary space is O(d) because in-place mutation with undo avoids a state copy per level.

limits.claim: No general sub-exponential algorithm exists for Hamiltonian path, n-queens or general SAT, and ETH rules out sub-exponential algorithms for monotone CNF with polynomial clauses, so the exponential behaviour is the best currently known rather than a weakness of the technique.
limits.detail: The exact worst-case node count for n-queens is not known in closed form: the 1.942^n rate is numerical, not proved.

supporting_structure.name: Incremental Constraint State with Exact Restoration
supporting_structure.rationale: Backtracking has no container to choose; its state is the partial solution plus bookkeeping that makes constraints O(1) to check. Two requirements are intrinsic to the technique: incremental counters (per-column and per-diagonal counts) rather than rescans, because that is what turns per-node cost from O(k) into O(1); and exact undo, because soundness of pruning depends on the state being precisely what it was on entry. Both belong to the technique rather than being auxiliary conveniences added to make it work.
